Founder: Michael Servetus (1511-1553) and later Unitarian churches
Summary: Unitarianism, in its historic form, teaches that God is one person and denies the Trinity and the pre-existence and full deity of Christ. It developed from 16th-century anti-Trinitarian movements into organized churches in Poland, Transylvania, England, and America.
Beliefs: God is one person; Jesus was a great teacher and moral example, not God incarnate; The Holy Spirit is not a distinct divine person; Reason and conscience guide interpretation of Scripture
Controversy: Debated throughout the Reformation and Enlightenment; historic confessions such as Westminster and the Nicene Creed were written in part to affirm Trinitarian faith against it
ChristianResponse: Historic churches affirm one God in three persons and salvation through Christ's death and resurrection, citing Matthew 28:19, John 20:28, and 1 Corinthians 15.
RelatedPeople: Michael Servetus; Fausto Sozzini; Joseph Priestley
